name: Isosorbide mononitrate

sources.citation: Genus Lifesciences. Isosorbide mononitrate immediate-release tablets. DailyMed; revised March 2025; set 0d739bf3-0672-4504-9064-b39d6b200b47. Verified 25 November 2026. US reference formulation.

Edenbridge/Dexcel isosorbide mononitrate extended-release tablets, repackaged by Coupler LLC. DailyMed; revised March 2025, updated December 2025; set 46b3030d-f492-da9d-e063-6294a90a31b3. US reference formulation.

revision_log.change: Faithful US-label summary with formulation-specific doses and kidney limitations; no inferred regimen or personal physician-review claim.
revision_log.approved_by: Codex source verification under the existing delegated workflow.

overview.mechanism: Relaxes vascular smooth muscle, reducing preload [[ISMNIR]].
uses: Angina prevention; oral onset is inadequate for aborting an acute attack [[ISMNIR,ISMNER]].

usual_adult_dose.dose: 20 mg twice daily, seven hours apart [[ISMNIR]].
Start 30 or 60 mg once each morning; after several days, increase to 120 mg if required. Rarely, 240 mg is required by the cited label [[ISMNER]].

dose_note: Immediate-release and extended-release schedules are separate. Do not crush or chew the cited ER tablets. Verify the specific Philippine formulation and insert; these regimens do not apply to isosorbide dinitrate [[ISMNIR,ISMNER]].
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; concurrent PDE5 inhibitors (such as sildenafil, tadalafil or vardenafil) or riociguat are contraindicated in the cited IR label [[ISMNIR]].

serious: Severe hypotension, potentially with paradoxical bradycardia or worsened angina [[ISMNIR]].

monitoring: Blood pressure, postural symptoms, volume status and adherence to the prescribed nitrate-free schedule [[ISMNIR,ISMNER]].

rows.findings: Continuous nitrate exposure produces tolerance; simply escalating doses does not restore reliable efficacy.
rows.limitations: Preserve the exact product schedule; neither formulation is an acute rescue nitrate.

rows.findings: IR labeling specifies no renal adjustment; ER labeling reports no accumulation in chronic renal failure.
rows.limitations: Hemodynamic tolerance and blood pressure still require assessment.
